answer: The mesa test I would run is Elevated confectioner licence with confectioners guild attestation: a licence the guild renews after kitchen audits, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a licence the guild renews after kitchen audits — so privacy survives, and the sparrow is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the island of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
